name: Business Administration and Management
overview: The first two years build the foundations: business management, microeconomics and macroeconomics, accounting, mathematics, statistics and marketing, followed by financial analysis, operations and business taxation. Teaching is practical, with Bloomberg terminals in the classroom, data-analysis software, and companies that co-teach selected subjects. In the final year you choose one of six pathways (economics, business law, business intelligence, business management, finance and accounting, or marketing), complete a compulsory internship and write a final project. Graduates go into financial analysis, consulting, operations, HR and strategy roles, or start their own ventures.

name: Business Administration and Management + Marketing
overview: This five-year route pairs a full business administration programme with marketing, starting from microeconomics, accounting, mathematics and company law, then moving into consumer behaviour, market research, pricing, product development, and digital and international marketing. You learn through group work, marketing simulators and workshops with industry professionals, and companies take part as co-teachers in some subjects. The last year brings a compulsory internship, a final thesis and electives such as e-commerce or sustainability, and exchange semesters at partner universities abroad are possible. Graduates work as marketing or product managers, business and financial analysts, consultants or entrepreneurs.

name: Computer Engineering
overview: The degree runs from programming, mathematics and physics in the first year through computer architecture, databases, networks and operating systems, to artificial intelligence, software engineering and enterprise information systems, and finally cybersecurity, web systems and business management. Small practical groups and laboratories, including a FabLab and virtual reality equipment, carry much of the teaching, and a compulsory internship and a final degree project close the course. A cybersecurity diploma can be added in years three and four. Graduates become software developers, systems analysts, IT security engineers, project managers or technology consultants.

name: Data Science and Engineering
overview: Mathematics, statistics and computer science are the base, moving from programming, databases and computer architecture in the first year to machine learning, big data, deep learning, optimisation and robotics in years two and three. Coursework is built around real projects and lab work with high-performance computing and cloud resources, with team problem solving supervised by experts from industry. In the later years you pick bioinformatics, business information systems or an open mix of electives, and finish with an internship and a final project. Graduates work as data scientists, data engineers, data architects, big data developers or AI systems designers.

name: Data Science and Data Engineering + Information Systems Engineering
overview: Two engineering degrees are combined, so the early years cover mathematics, statistics, physics and programming, then machine learning, cloud infrastructure, neural networks, databases and software engineering, and later Bayesian analysis, distributed computing and the management of information systems. Real-world projects supervised by industry experts run through the course, along with labs for high-performance computing, virtual reality and data analysis, and a compulsory internship in the fourth year. You complete the business information systems track and can add bioinformatics or open electives. Graduates work as data scientists, data engineers, software engineers, security engineers, IT directors or consultants.

name: Dentistry
overview: The five years move from biology, anatomy, physiology, biochemistry and psychology into microbiology, pharmacology, biomaterials and head and neck anatomy, then paediatric dentistry, oral pathology, orthodontics, prosthetics and surgery, and finally periodontics, implantology, endodontics and maxillofacial surgery. Clinical training is central: students practise first in a simulation hospital and on a university polyclinic, and from the third year treat real patients under supervision. Electives include practice management and oral microbiota. Graduates work in private practice or hospital dentistry, research, teaching and public health.

name: Physiotherapy
overview: Anatomy, biology, physiology and biomechanics lead into pathology, manual therapy and musculoskeletal physiotherapy, then neurology, cardiorespiratory care, paediatrics and research methods. Most of the training is practical: simulated treatment rooms and a clinical simulation hospital come first, a university polyclinic offers real-patient practice, and external hospital and clinic placements begin in the second year. The final year has intensive clinical rotations and a capstone project, and electives include sports physiotherapy and intensive care. Graduates work in hospitals, primary care, sports clubs, specialist centres, research or their own practice.

name: International Relations and the European Union
overview: You study geopolitics, the theory and history of international relations, international public law, the history and institutions of the European Union, and diplomacy and negotiation, together with a modern language. Later years add EU law, human rights, the single market, international trade and regional studies, with electives such as migration and asylum, and a final dissertation. Teaching uses case resolution, simulations and debates, and one semester abroad is compulsory. A second degree in law, economics or journalism can be added. Graduates go into European institutions, diplomacy, NGOs, journalism, consulting and international departments of companies.

name: Advertising and Public Relations
overview: The first years cover writing, art and design, photography, advertising principles and communication theory, then creative thinking, public relations techniques, radio, video and digital production. Third year turns to advertising creativity, brand management and research methods, and the last year brings an internship, a final project and electives such as campaign planning or corporate reputation. Students work in the HUB, a communication and advertising agency run inside the school, and use TV and radio studios, photography labs and editing suites. Graduates become creative directors, account executives, copywriters, community managers and brand managers.

name: Audiovisual Communication
overview: The first year mixes contemporary history, art and design, photography, writing and communication theory; later years move to radio and podcast production, television and video, audiovisual narrative, cinematography, screenwriting and editing. The final year adds digital composition, sound and multi-camera production, an internship with media or production companies, and a final project. Students work on content projects in an in-house agency called the HUB and use television and radio studios, post-production rooms and photography labs from the start. Graduates work as producers, directors, scriptwriters and editors in television, radio and film, or in corporate communication and press offices.

name: Digital Communication
overview: After a first year of photography, writing, communication theory and the basics of advertising, the course adds graphic communication, web programming, radio, podcasts and television, then social media management, brand reputation, strategic communication and data analytics. Teaching is learning by doing, in a student-run space called the HUB and in editing suites, TV and radio studios and photography labs, with free loan of cameras and recorders. Electives cover virtual and augmented reality, gamification and transmedia storytelling, and the last year has an external internship and a final project. Graduates work as social media, community or brand managers, UX designers, content creators and digital marketers.

name: Journalism
overview: Writing, photography, communication theory and contemporary history open the course, followed by radio and podcast production, television and video, journalistic editing and documentation, then audiovisual journalism, ethics, communication law, data visualisation and international relations. Students train by doing, using two TV studios, two radio studios and editing rooms, and publishing through the school's HUB platform. An external internship at a Spanish media outlet and a final project come in the fourth year, with elective strands in sports, political and economic, cultural and scientific, or socio-religious journalism. Graduates work as journalists and editors, community managers, press officers and photojournalists.

name: Fundamentals of Architecture
overview: You start with drawing, geometry, materials, form analysis and structures, then move into design studios, building construction, urban design, structural analysis and environmental and electrical systems. Teaching is studio-based and project-driven, with workshops that mimic professional practice from the first year, and an optional internship at architecture practices. The final years add advanced design projects and construction detailing, with a choice between a Building Design mention and a Building Technology mention, and a final thesis. Graduates go into independent practice, urban planning, heritage restoration, construction management, BIM, sustainability consulting or research.

name: Interior Design
overview: The first year covers drawing, design basics, representation systems, light and colour and computer-assisted drawing; later years add design studios, construction materials and systems, retail and domestic design, public spaces, lighting and electrical design and refurbishment techniques. In year four come digital fabrication, scenography, furniture, garden and landscape design, exhibition design, project management and a final project. Learning is project-based, with 3D modelling and rendering, a FabLab, model workshops and a virtual reality lab, plus a mandatory professional internship. Graduates work as interior designers, project managers, design directors and retail consultants in studios and architecture firms.

name: Fashion Design and Management and its Industry
overview: The first year brings design basics, textiles, fashion sociology, pattern making, art history, marketing and management economics, and later years add brand identity, digital design tools, product design, communication strategy, business strategy and sustainability. Four project workshops build from creative experiments to a full collection, and teaching takes place in design studios, animation studios and innovation labs on a creativity campus, with links to fashion companies, shows and fairs. A mandatory external internship and a degree project close the course. Graduates work as fashion designers, product managers, creative directors, trend consultants, brand managers and merchandisers, or start their own labels.

name: Bachelor's Degree in Business Administration and Management [ADE] (E-2 English)
overview: The first year covers management, accounting, business and financial mathematics, data analysis and microeconomics, and later years add statistics, marketing, macroeconomics, operations, organisational behaviour, corporate finance, strategy, market research and human resources. In the final year you choose electives in marketing, management, finance and accounting, or economics, complete a compulsory company placement and write a final project. Exchanges at partner universities are common, and double degrees with universities in the United States and Europe are offered. Graduates work in management, strategy consulting, corporate finance, marketing, international trade or their own ventures.

name: Bachelor's Degree in Business Analytics (E-8)
overview: Algebra, calculus, programming, economics and business fundamentals come first, followed by statistics, databases, financial accounting and introductory machine learning, then big data, cybersecurity, marketing analytics and quantitative finance. The last year adds deep learning and artificial intelligence, electives such as fintech, customer intelligence, sustainability measurement and supply chain analytics, a compulsory work placement and a final project. Case studies drawn from real business settings run through the course, and a double degree with international relations is available. Graduates become data analysts, machine learning specialists, strategy consultants or investment advisers.

name: Bachelor's Degree in International Relations
overview: The course starts with law, political theory and the history of international relations, then adds comparative political systems, public international law, geopolitics, international political economy and climate governance. Later years cover international organisations, security, European Union institutions, regional studies of Africa and Latin America, trade and investment, and end with a final project. Language training runs for up to four years, work placements are available, and you can spend a semester at a partner university. Double degrees run through programmes in the Americas and Asia-Pacific. Graduates work in diplomacy, international organisations, think tanks and consultancies.

name: Dual Degree in Global Communication and International Relations
overview: Two degrees share one curriculum, with early years in political theory, international relations, communication theory, law and economics, plus two further languages. The entire third year is spent at a university abroad, with a three-week immersion in Brussels on the EU institutions. Years four and five let you specialise in economics and business, law and diplomacy, or security and human rights, with external internships and a thesis for each degree. A second exchange in the final year is optional. Graduates work as diplomats, international civil servants, policy analysts, communications directors and consultants.

name: Business Management and Administration (BMA)
overview: The programme covers how a company works across its departments: finance, marketing plans, strategic business planning, people management, and the legal, economic and social factors that shape a firm. Recent content brings in digital transformation, sustainability and data analysis. Classes mix theory with case studies, oral presentations, debates, management simulators and company visits, with managers bringing real problems into the classroom, and compulsory university-managed internships. You can add a complement in digital business intelligence, international management skills, or innovation and entrepreneurship, depending on campus. Graduates take roles across a wide range of sectors and organisations.

name: BMA + International Relations
overview: Business administration is combined with international relations, so you study how companies are managed alongside the economic, political and cultural forces that link states and firms worldwide. You learn to read business data and the international situation together, to build strategies that account for the environment, and to manage teams and projects in public and private organisations. Teaching mixes case studies, debates, simulations, company visits and speakers from industry, with a compulsory period abroad and compulsory internships arranged by the university. Graduates work in international management in companies and public bodies.

name: Bachelor of Business Administration – BBA
overview: The degree builds a general management foundation and adds marketing, finance, operations and human resources, so you can weigh each decision across the whole company; AI tools and data analytics are woven into the subjects. You learn by solving real cases, simulating the creation and running of companies, and taking part in business games and capstone projects, taught partly by executives from companies. A semester abroad and a semester-long internship in the fourth year are compulsory, and you can choose a minor such as data analytics, finance, consulting, entrepreneurship, marketing, or global leadership and diversity. A dual programme with partners in China or Canada is also offered.

name: Bachelor in Business and Artificial Intelligence
overview: Business fundamentals are joined to a technical core in advanced mathematics, machine learning, deep learning, computational modelling, generative AI, natural language processing, computer vision, software development for business and cloud solutions, along with ethics, legal frameworks and human-centred AI. You work on hackathons, datathons and boot camps, and with classmates you simulate creating and running companies using AI strategies. An internship is compulsory, in Spain or abroad, with a solidarity placement in developing countries as an option, and a semester exchange comes in the fourth year. The result is a hybrid profile linking business units and technical teams.

name: Bachelor in Global Governance, Economics & Legal Order
overview: The course combines economics, international relations, international law and public policy, covering legal systems, human rights, cybersecurity, macroeconomics, geopolitics and international institutions. In the second year you choose a track, either economics and finance or international relations and public policy. Learning is hands-on, through practical cases, international moot courts, model United Nations sessions and capstone modules based on a European Investment Bank project, with a compulsory semester abroad. Internships in the third and fourth years can be at international organisations such as the World Bank or UNESCO, and language electives include Spanish, French, German, Arabic and Mandarin.

name: Bachelor in Transformational Leadership and Social Impact
overview: Business, humanities and technology are taught together, with business tools for sustainability and social impact (entrepreneurship, marketing, finance, operations, strategy, design thinking), humanities such as philosophy, anthropology, sociology and psychology, and AI and big data applied to human problems. Much of the work happens in cross-cutting collaborative projects, in a dedicated classroom, a Fab Lab and company settings, with a compulsory internship and an optional solidarity internship. Cohorts are small, at around fifty students, and international experiences in Europe and Asia are part of the course. Graduates aim to become impact entrepreneurs or managers working for social impact.

name: Double Degree Bachelor of Business Administration & Business and Artificial Intelligence
overview: Two degrees run side by side: a full business administration programme and a technical programme in business and artificial intelligence, giving a base in management plus a STEM foundation in machine learning and AI. Learning by doing includes hackathons, datathons and boot camps, tech dialogues with experts from industry and academia, and situated projects in which you apply AI in a real context and weigh its social and environmental effects. An internship is compulsory, with a solidarity option abroad. Graduates move into areas such as finance, marketing, operations, logistics or human resources, bridging business and technology teams.

name: Double Degree in Business Administration + Bachelor in Global Governance, Economics & Legal Order
overview: Management is studied together with geopolitics, international law, economics and public policy from the first year, and you finish with a business degree plus a track in economics and finance or in international relations and public policy. In the second and third years, teams carry out strategic consulting projects for partner companies, and learning also comes from moot courts, model United Nations sessions, business simulations and an annual capstone with the European Investment Bank. Exchanges, optional study experiences abroad and a study tour make it the most international of the dual programmes, and internships are compulsory. Graduates can lead in firms and institutions that deal with global politics and economics.

name: Bachelor in Applied Mathematics
overview: The first two years lay a common mathematical foundation, and in years three and four you specialise in industrial mathematics, artificial intelligence or financial mathematics, depending on availability. The course trains you to turn real situations into mathematical models and optimise decisions under constraints, with theory, numerical work and coding side by side; you also learn to write in LaTeX, present scientific posters and draft manuscripts, with a touch of quantum computing. A capstone project closes the degree, and internships and exchanges are encouraged. Graduates go into roles such as data scientist, machine learning engineer, quantitative trader or cryptography specialist, or into research.

name: Bachelor in Architectural Studies
overview: Studied entirely in Segovia, the programme is built around design studios that copy the way a firm or agency works, plus a Fab Lab for digital fabrication and a bio lab for materials. Alongside core architecture courses you take modules in design entrepreneurship, experimentation and management. In the second semesters of years two, three and four you work in studios, magazines, museums, NGOs or architecture firms around the world, and an optional diploma in product, graphic or interior design can be added. The degree leads to the one-year master's in architecture needed for professional licensure in Spain and across the European Union.

name: Bachelor in Behavior and Social Sciences
overview: Human behaviour is studied together with business and analytics, so you learn why people think and choose as they do, how organisations change, and how to measure and predict behaviour with data. The practical curriculum includes projects with real businesses, and you choose one of two elective tracks: human-centred consulting, where you solve challenges for real clients, or marketing and talent strategy, built around an AI-powered business simulation. The first year can be spent in Segovia before moving to Madrid. Graduates work as consultants, HR and talent managers, consumer behaviour analysts, market researchers and customer experience designers.

name: Bachelor in Business Administration
overview: Fundamentals courses in finance, marketing and the other core business disciplines are combined with practical courses in which you carry out projects for real companies and organisations, and with broadening electives in humanities and technology. You build business plans and start-up projects, and track your own progress on a personal dashboard. The first two years can be spent in Segovia, with years three and four in Madrid, or all four in Madrid. Graduates become consultants, financial managers, marketing managers or entrepreneurs.

name: Global Bachelor in Business Administration
overview: You spend four years in four places: the first in Madrid, the second in Singapore, the third in Dubai, and the fourth in Madrid or New York City. Each stop builds on business foundations in finance, management and economics, through practical projects, business sprints, labs, corporate challenges and regional business treks, plus non-credit sessions on geopolitics and geoeconomics. In the final year you either graduate in Madrid with one of eight concentrations or take a 3+1 pathway in New York that adds a master's. Graduates aim for roles such as global strategy consultant, business development manager, global marketing manager or cross-border entrepreneur.

name: Bachelor in Communication and Digital Media
overview: Strategic and critical analysis of cultural trends, audiences and media environments sits alongside creativity taught as a method, through design thinking, semiotics and narrative construction. You build fluency in written, visual, audio and interactive content, treating platforms as cultural environments rather than just channels. Hands-on projects take place in the MediaLab, where students produce content, test strategies and defend their choices with evidence. The first years can be spent in Segovia, building programming and technical skills, before moving to Madrid. Graduates go into advertising, branding, digital content, media strategy, and brand and marketing management.

name: Bachelor in Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence
overview: The core is engineering-focused: programming, algorithms, data structures, software engineering, systems architecture and applied mathematics, joined with machine learning, AI and robotics. Teaching follows a project-based tech-studio approach with industry collaboration and technical experimentation from the first year. You can start in Segovia and finish in Madrid, close to the city's technology companies and start-ups, or study in Madrid throughout. Graduates become software, machine learning, AI, cloud, cybersecurity or site reliability engineers, systems architects, technical product managers or research scientists.

name: Bachelor in Data and Business Analytics
overview: You learn to collect, manage and analyse data with current analytics tools, and to turn the results into decisions for companies and institutions. Teaching is applied, with datathons, challenges and practical class projects tackling complex real-world problems, and the course develops a critical way of breaking problems down. The first part can be spent in Segovia before moving to Madrid, or all four years can be in Madrid. Graduates become data scientists, business intelligence and analytics consultants, data solutions architects or data officers.

name: Bachelor in Design
overview: A broad design foundation covers the history of design, drawing for analysis and communication, 3D visualisation, social sciences, sustainability and modern technology, combined with a business side that includes business plans, sales processes and project management. Learning is project-based, with real prototypes and a Design Council in which professional partners share projects in progress for students and faculty to research and answer. The first two years are in Segovia and the last two in Madrid, and you can add an optional diploma in visual communication, product design or interior design. Graduates work as graphic, product, interior or service designers, design strategists and creative consultants.

name: Bachelor in Economics
overview: Econometrics, political science, applied analytics, behavioural science and technology are studied together, including the effects of automation, e-platforms, artificial intelligence and big data on the economy, and behavioural and experimental economics. The first three years build the foundations, and in the fourth you specialise in either country, sector and policy analysis or economic and financial analysis for business. The first two years can be in Segovia before moving to Madrid. Graduates work as economic consultants, financial market analysts, policy developers, equity analysts and government research consultants.

name: Bachelor in Environmental Sciences for Sustainability
overview: Biology, chemistry, physics, geology, ecology and data science are studied together with environmental policy and governance, without having to specialise early. Teaching is science-first and practical, with fieldwork in the countryside around Segovia, lab experimentation, quantitative analysis and project work with stakeholders from industry, government and society. The programme looks closely at topics such as the energy transition and the green economy, and all four years take place in Segovia. Graduates become water resource and ecosystem analysts, environmental data analysts, renewable energy and impact analysts, or climate risk analysts.

name: Bachelor in Fashion Design
overview: Project-based design studios guide you through making garments, accessories and collections while confronting the material, economic, social and cultural factors behind them. Sustainability, fashion management, the blend of traditional craft with new technology, and entrepreneurship run through the course, and faculty are working professionals in the industry. The first two years are in Segovia and the last two in Madrid, and you can add a diploma in product design, visual communication or interior design. Graduates go on to found their own labels or work as stylists, textile designers, costume designers, sustainability consultants and virtual fashion designers.

name: Bachelor in Humanities
overview: Traditional disciplines such as history, philosophy and art are combined with digital tools including algorithmic thinking, coding and data mining, so critical thinking is paired with quantitative skills. Faculty include humanities scholars and practitioners from the digital field, and the degree develops creativity, communication, ethics, foresight and cultural awareness. The first two years are in Segovia and the last two in Madrid, with exchange options and an immersion experience in Paris. Graduates work as technology ethics consultants, cultural institution managers, content creators, UX researchers, heritage experts or game creative directors.

name: Bachelor in International Relations
overview: The curriculum is organised around the five themes of the UN's sustainable development agenda (people, planet, prosperity, peace and partnership) and gives a grounding in the economic, political and cultural sides of global problems. Learning is practice-based, with case studies and policy-lab seminars, and a partnership with the United Nations System Staff College brings UN courses, practitioners, summer research programmes, mentoring and capstone projects. An exchange programme is part of the degree, and the first two years can be in Segovia. Graduates go into the UN and other multilateral bodies, diplomacy, consultancies, NGOs, think tanks, political parties and humanitarian work.

name: Bachelor of Laws (LL.B.)
overview: The degree is taught in English with a comparative approach to international, European and transnational law, and you can follow a track in international business law, human rights and social justice, or digital law and technology. A concentration in Spanish business law is available in Spanish. Practice runs through the course in a mentoring programme, a legal clinic, hands-on capstone work and professional internships at law firms, and exchanges and dual degrees with partner law schools can lead to an LL.M. alongside the bachelor. Graduates work as corporate and international lawyers, legal advisers to NGOs, or legal tech specialists.

name: Bachelor in Philosophy, Politics, Law and Economics (PPLE)
overview: Philosophy, politics, law and economics are studied together, with the freedom to specialise in one or two of them, so you gain critical analysis, logical argument and ways of weighing governance, legal and economic questions. Learning combines theory with case studies, seminars, consultancy projects, international competitions and real-life projects. The first two years can be in Segovia before moving to Madrid. Graduates go into policy making, think tanks, political advice, law, strategy advice, NGOs, government and international organisations.

name: Bachelor in Political Science
overview: Political science, public policy, public administration and leadership are combined to show how power, institutions and governance shape societies, with attention to regulation, public affairs, democratic resilience and the effects of AI, data analytics, GovTech and cybersecurity on policy. Teaching is practical, through policy labs, consulting-style projects, study trips and real-world projects, with partnerships involving GESDA, Google and the International Telecommunication Union. The first years can be in Segovia, with exchange options. Graduates move into public policy, public affairs, government relations, consulting, advocacy and research.

name: Dual Degree Bachelor in Business Administration and Bachelor of Laws (LL.B.)
overview: Law and business are taught as one integrated plan: the first year gives foundations in both fields, then later years go deeper into economics, globalisation, entrepreneurship and corporate law, with a comparative-law approach and an international focus. The two schools involved, the business school and the law school, share teaching, and you graduate with two undergraduate diplomas. The programme is taught in Madrid. Graduates go into roles such as corporate lawyer in multinationals, legal adviser to international companies, project finance lawyer, investment banking associate or entrepreneur.

name: Dual Degree Bachelor of Laws (LL.B.) and Bachelor in International Relations
overview: Law and international relations are merged into one study plan: the first year gives a broad base in both, and later years turn to globalisation, international affairs, conflict resolution and public law, building negotiation, crisis management and persuasion skills. The programme draws on the law school and the school of politics, economics and global affairs, is taught in Madrid, and ends in two undergraduate diplomas. It suits students aiming at public-sector legal work. Graduates become diplomats, human rights lawyers, foreign policy consultants, international criminal or arbitration lawyers and NGO advocates.

name: Dual Degree in Business Administration & Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence
overview: Computer science foundations in programming, algorithms, data structures, software engineering and mathematics are studied alongside business strategy, management and entrepreneurship, with artificial intelligence and modern computing linked to how they change organisations. Industry professionals teach on the programme, and Madrid's technology and business community is close at hand. Graduates aim to bridge engineering and business as entrepreneurs, consultants, machine learning engineers, blockchain developers or digital strategists.

name: Dual Degree in Business Administration & Data and Business Analytics
overview: Management is combined with data: you learn statistical tools to formulate and analyse data, and use them to guide business decisions and add value in sectors from finance to healthcare. Faculty come from both the business and data fields, and you can choose from internships, exchange programmes and other professional initiatives. You earn two undergraduate diplomas. Graduates work as fintech specialists, customer insight directors, marketing intelligence managers, talent analytics leads or trading specialists.

name: Dual Degree in Business Administration & Design
overview: Business administration and design are blended into one programme in which you work with professors and industry professionals on how a company operates and how design shapes products, services and human experience. It is hands-on and aimed at creative students who want to build human-centred solutions inside businesses. You graduate with two undergraduate diplomas. Graduates become innovation managers, strategy and innovation consultants, creative officers, user experience designers, customer experience researchers, business model designers or brand strategists.

name: Dual Degree in Business Administration & Fashion Design
overview: A five-year programme in which fashion design and business administration run together, covering industry trends, supply chains and branding, with sustainability, circularity, inclusivity and social responsibility at the centre. The design side is practical, based on making, testing and critiquing in a fab lab, a fashion studio and a tech lab, balanced by practical business projects, and there are international exchange opportunities. Graduates become founders and creative directors of their own labels, fashion buyers, brand managers, sustainability managers or marketing managers.

name: Dual Degree in Business Administration & Humanities
overview: The analytical, digital and critical-thinking skills of the humanities are joined with the management and quantitative tools of a business degree. You study subjects such as history, philosophy, literature and ethics, to read patterns of cause and consequence, assess information critically and communicate clearly, alongside business training. Faculty include scholars and practitioners from both worlds. You graduate with two degrees. Graduates work as strategy consultants, marketing and communications specialists, business development managers, corporate affairs specialists or entrepreneurs.

name: Dual Degree in Business Administration & International Relations
overview: Business administration is paired with international relations, giving a base in business, geopolitics and current affairs and a view of how companies and states deal with one another across borders. The programme is practice-based, with specialised training in negotiation, strategy and public speaking, and theory is put to work in summer internships or university labs, with exchanges open at a large network of partner institutions. It is taught in Madrid and ends in two undergraduate diplomas. Graduates go on to consult for international organisations, work in multinationals or NGOs, or become social entrepreneurs.

name: Dual Degree in Business Administration and Political Science
overview: Business strategy and political science are studied side by side, to show how companies, governments and international institutions interact and how political decisions move markets. Hands-on projects, policy labs and collaborations with organisations such as GESDA, Google and the International Telecommunication Union take up issues like AI governance, digital transformation, sustainability, international cooperation and geopolitical risk. The aim is a graduate who can shape corporate strategy, read regulatory and political change, advise organisations or build ventures with an international reach.

name: Dual Degree in Economics & Applied Mathematics
overview: The economics half covers econometrics, political science, applied analytics, behavioural science and technology, while the mathematics half covers calculus, linear algebra, statistics, differential equations, mathematical modelling, programming and machine learning. You learn to apply mathematical language to real economic problems using various programming languages. The result is a profile suited to finance, economic consulting, data analysis and sustainable development. Graduates become financial data analysts, econometric analysts, risk management consultants, financial modelling specialists or data scientists in economic analysis.

name: Dual Degree in Economics & International Relations
overview: Economics, history, politics and international relations are combined, with an emphasis on how states, businesses, international organisations, NGOs and think tanks relate to one another. You learn to design and lead strategic policy for global problems, drawing on digital platforms and emerging technologies and on advanced analytical tools. Learning includes partnerships that let students learn by doing, and exchanges abroad. Graduates work in international financial institutions, development banks, policy making, think tanks, economic research, journalism or social entrepreneurship.

name: Bachelor's Degree in Artificial Intelligence
overview: The course builds the cognitive, mathematical and algorithmic foundations of reasoning and learning, then moves into natural language processing, computer vision, data analysis, robotics and autonomous agents, along with the ethical, legal and social side of using AI. Teaching is hands-on, with project work and case-based projects carried out with companies, and two nearby research centres, the Computer Vision Centre and the Artificial Intelligence Research Institute, are involved. Faculty come from several university departments. Graduates design and run AI applications in public administration, healthcare, finance and media, work in project management and consulting, or go into research.

name: Bachelor's Degree in Business Administration - English
overview: The core is business management: accounting, marketing, finance, strategy and the organisation of companies, studied in small groups and with the aim of building business English alongside the managerial skills. In the fourth year you can complete an optional work placement in an English-speaking environment, and Erasmus and university exchanges are encouraged, especially to English-speaking countries. A final project closes the degree. Graduates work as financial directors, marketing managers, tax consultants, auditors, business consultants, investment analysts or entrepreneurs, and the degree also leads to public administration.

name: Bachelor's Degree in Economics - English
overview: Economics is studied entirely in English over four years, with the aim of making sound decisions in public bodies and private businesses. In the final year you follow an itinerary that lets you specialise in the area that interests you most, and an optional work placement with English-speaking employers is available, arranged with Barcelona Activa. Exchanges run through Erasmus+, exchanges within Spain and the university's worldwide mobility programme, and a final project is required. Graduates work as economic and financial analysts, consultants, data analysts and policy designers in public administration, banking and companies, or go into research.

name: Bachelor's Degree in Tourism - English
overview: The degree covers the business management and organisation of tourist activities, destinations, services and resources, with attention to innovation and sustainability, and builds proficiency in several foreign languages. You choose one of three tracks: tourism business management, tourism marketing, planning and digitalisation, or hotel management. Practice includes hundreds of placement positions, work in a hotel on campus, Erasmus exchanges, work-experience placements and a double degree option with a university of applied sciences in Austria. A final project closes the degree. Graduates work in tourism and hospitality marketing, revenue management, events, travel platforms, product creation, consulting or their own ventures.

name: Bachelor's degree in English Studies
overview: The degree is taught entirely in English and builds an advanced command of the language together with the study of literary texts from different periods, genres and cultural settings, and a grounding in applied linguistics and its uses. Typical courses combine English language, English-language literature and linguistics, and students write a final degree project. In the fourth year, external placements give practice in a professional setting where English is used. Graduates usually teach English in schools, secondary institutes and language schools, go on to university teaching and research, or work in public administration and in publishing and cultural industries.

name: Bachelor in Biomedical Sciences
overview: The first year covers cell biology, biophysics, chemistry, biostatistics, microbiology, molecular biology, biochemistry, genetics and histology, followed by anatomy, physiology, immunology, biotechnology and toxicology, and later epidemiology, general pathology, experimental models and pathology of cancer, infectious and cardiovascular disease. Dedicated laboratory courses run in the third and fourth years, external internships are available, and a research-based bachelor thesis closes the degree. You can follow a voluntary itinerary in microbiology, cardiology or oncology. Graduates work as laboratory technicians, biomedical researchers, quality control specialists and diagnostic staff, or go on to master's study and research.

name: Bachelor in Neuroscience
overview: The first year lays foundations in biophysics, chemistry, genetics, mathematics, biostatistics, biochemistry, immunology and neurobiology; then come neuroanatomy, cellular neurophysiology, cognition, laboratory techniques and programming, and later neurological and psychiatric disease, neuroimaging, brain-machine interfaces and neuropharmacology. Laboratory work runs throughout, internships can be done at research institutes, hospitals and pharmaceutical or technology companies, and a bachelor thesis closes the degree. Electives let you lean toward computational neuroscience, neurodegeneration, pain or toxicology. Graduates work as research scientists and healthcare technicians, or continue to postgraduate study.

name: Bachelor's Degree in Primary Education
overview: The first year covers developmental and educational psychology, the theory and sociology of education, inclusive education and digital skills, and later years turn to teaching Spanish, mathematics, English, social and experimental sciences, physical education, music and arts. You are in schools from the second year on, with placements that grow longer each year, and a bachelor thesis closes the degree. Teaching is bilingual in English and Spanish, and you can follow a mention in English language teaching or in special educational needs. Graduates qualify as primary school teachers and can continue to a master's in secondary teacher training.

name: Bachelor in Business Administration
overview: The first year covers economics, mathematics, accounting, statistics, law and communication, followed by macroeconomics, organisational behaviour, financial economics and commercial law, then marketing, financial management and strategy. The last year brings strategic and operations management, electives and a bachelor thesis, and external academic internships are available with a large network of companies. Electives let you lean toward financial accounting, general management or marketing management, and an English-language group runs on the Getafe campus. Graduates work as marketing managers, financial analysts, HR managers, auditors, consultants and logistics directors.

name: Bachelor in Economics
overview: The first two years build the foundations in mathematics, statistics, microeconomics and macroeconomics, and the last two give you wide freedom in electives, including three optional intensification paths: microeconomics, macroeconomics, or quantitative techniques and applied economics. External internships are available through the university's company network, a bachelor thesis is required, and teaching is offered in both Spanish and English with exchanges through Erasmus. Faculty research feeds into the teaching. Graduates work in economic consulting, financial analysis, risk assessment, public administration and international organisations.

name: Bachelor in Finance and Accounting
overview: The first year covers financial mathematics, business administration, economics, introductory accounting, statistics and law, then financial accounting, financial economics and derivatives, and later cost management, risk management, financial statement analysis, auditing and corporate governance, with electives such as sustainable finance and big data analytics. Professional internships with banks and audit firms are available, a bachelor thesis closes the degree, and teaching is bilingual in Spanish and English. Graduates work as financial analysts, risk managers, auditors, consultants and civil servants in regulatory bodies.

name: Bachelor in International Studies
overview: The first year covers micro- and macroeconomics, comparative politics, sociology, world politics, statistics and legal methods, followed by international political economy, public law, international organisations, security and conflict resolution, then human rights, international finance and policy evaluation. Electives let you focus on development cooperation, trade, geopolitics, democracy or security policy. A bachelor thesis closes the degree, external internships are possible, and exchanges run through Erasmus. Graduates work in multinational companies, international organisations, NGOs, think tanks, public administration, political consulting and investigative journalism.

name: Bachelor in Management and Technology
overview: Management and technology are taught together: the first year covers economics, mathematics, accounting, programming and IT basics, followed by databases, operations, digital business and statistics, then big data, AI in business, machine learning and strategy, and finally cybersecurity, financial management and a thesis. Electives let you focus on digital marketing, ERP systems, supply chain or innovation management, and students gain training in SAP applications. Internships are available through a large network of companies, and exchanges run through Erasmus. Graduates work as economists, business intelligence analysts, ICT specialists and management consultants.

name: Bachelor in Urban Sustainability Studies (joint with european universities)
overview: A three-year degree shared with partner universities in Belgium, the Netherlands, Finland, the United Kingdom, Poland and Croatia. The first year covers comparative sociology, economics, climate science, urban development, statistics, environmental technology and cultural geography; the next two years are built from three minors on topics such as urban health, sustainable business, smart cities, urban ecology and sustainable tourism, chosen across partner universities. You work in project-based Challenge Teams solving real sustainability problems, spend at least two periods at partner universities, and write a bachelor thesis. The degree leads to specialised master's programmes.

name: Dual Bachelor in International Studies and Business Administration
overview: Taught in English over five and a half years, the dual degree starts with economics, mathematics, law, politics and introductory accounting, then moves to international trade, strategic management, marketing, financial management, international organisations, globalisation and security studies. Multidisciplinary seminars on international studies run alongside, you write a bachelor thesis for each degree, and electives include international security policy and sustainable finance. External internships are available at companies and organisations, and Erasmus exchanges are possible. Graduates work as marketing directors, export managers, financial analysts, or in business intelligence, public administration, NGOs, think tanks and diplomacy.

name: Dual Bachelor in International Studies and Economics
overview: Taught in English on the Getafe campus over five and a half years, the dual degree starts with mathematics, economics, statistics, business administration and politics, then adds macroeconomics, microeconomic theory, econometrics and financial economics alongside public law, international political economy and trade. Later electives cover innovation, development, security policy and emerging countries, and you write a bachelor thesis for each degree. Programming and data analysis are built in, external internships are available, and Erasmus exchanges are possible. Graduates work as financial analysts, strategic consultants and tax inspectors, or in international organisations, NGOs, public administration and think tanks.

name: Bachelor in Aerospace Engineering
overview: After a first year of mathematics, physics, programming and chemistry, you study fluid mechanics, aerodynamics, propulsion, structures, materials, thermal engineering and flight mechanics, then advanced design and control. In the last years you specialise in aerospace vehicles (aircraft design, aeroelasticity, flight mechanics) or aerospace propulsion (turbomachinery, combustion, rocket motors). Classes are small and practical, with laboratory work, optional professional internships and a bachelor thesis. Graduates work in the design, manufacture, certification and maintenance of aircraft and spacecraft, and in air navigation systems.

name: Bachelor in Applied Mathematics
overview: The first year covers linear algebra, calculus, programming and digital skills, then differential equations, numerical methods, mechanics and probability, and later functional analysis, optimisation, game theory, stochastic calculus and mathematical biology. In the final year you choose among many electives, such as machine learning, cryptography, financial mathematics, biophysics, quantum physics and robotics, and write a bachelor thesis. Teaching is in English, internships are available and Erasmus exchanges are possible. Graduates enter technology and software companies, financial institutions, AI, aerospace, research centres, biotechnology and data consulting.

name: Bachelor in Artificial Intelligence
overview: The first year covers programming, linear algebra, calculus, discrete mathematics, logic, probability and statistics, then data structures, automata and formal languages, databases and early machine learning, and later deep learning, knowledge-based systems, cloud computing, generative AI, ethics and security. The last year brings computer vision, robotics, natural language processing, a capstone AI project and a bachelor thesis, with electives from quantum computing to AI in healthcare. Part-time professionals teach on the degree, internships are possible, and English-taught teaching is offered on the Leganes campus. Graduates work as AI engineers, machine learning specialists and research scientists.

name: Bachelor in Biomedical Engineering
overview: The first year covers mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and programming with an introduction to bioengineering, followed by biochemistry, electronics, statistics, control engineering and fluid mechanics in biomedicine, and later medical instrumentation, physiology, robotics, tissue engineering, biomaterials and medical image processing. Strong laboratory work, internships in hospitals, companies and research centres, and a bachelor thesis feature, and you can concentrate on tissue engineering, biomedical imaging, or instrumentation and medical devices. Graduates work in pharmaceutical and biotech firms, hospitals, consulting and research on medical devices, diagnostics and new therapies.

name: Bachelor in Data Science and Engineering
overview: Mathematics, statistics, computer science and telecommunications are combined, starting with linear algebra, calculus, programming, probability and data analysis, then statistical learning, databases, machine learning, signal processing and cybersecurity, and later deep learning, optimisation, Bayesian analysis and web and mobile development. A data science project, hands-on labs, optional internships and a bachelor thesis feature, and electives cover natural language processing, computer vision, healthcare, bioinformatics and robotics. Graduates work as data scientists, data engineers and machine learning engineers in finance, healthcare, automotive, retail and technology.

name: Bachelor in Energy Engineering
overview: The first year covers linear algebra, calculus, physics, programming and communication, then industrial automation, electrical fundamentals, thermal engineering and fluid mechanics, followed by wind and solar energy, power generation, transmission and energy economics, and finally nuclear energy and demand management. The degree is taught in English with well-equipped laboratories, internships with energy companies and a bachelor thesis, and electives include energy in buildings, transport and smart grids. Graduates work on sizing thermal and renewable generation, energy efficiency, auditing and energy market analysis.

name: Bachelor in Engineering Physics
overview: The first year covers mathematics, physics, chemistry, programming and statistics, then quantum physics, mechanics and relativity, electromagnetism, optics and materials science, followed by statistical physics, fluid mechanics, electronic engineering and instrumentation, and finally quantum computation, biomaterials and nanoelectronics. Lab practicals are held in small groups, internships are available and a bachelor thesis closes the degree. Electives range from quantum technologies, nanomaterials and plasma physics to renewable energy, robotics and control. Graduates work in research centres, biotechnology, quantum computing, nanotechnology, photonics and the space industry.

name: Bachelor in Mathematics and Computing
overview: Mathematics and computer science are studied together, from linear algebra, calculus, discrete mathematics and programming, through numerical methods, complex analysis, cryptography, automata, algorithms and artificial intelligence, to differential equations, optimisation, databases and language processors. Final-year electives include machine learning, financial mathematics, parallel programming and stochastic processes, and a bachelor thesis closes the degree. Laboratory work runs throughout, external internships are available and exchanges run through Erasmus. Graduates work as quantitative analysts, software developers, scientific computing specialists, researchers and consultants.

name: Bachelor in Robotics Engineering
overview: After mathematics, physics, programming and an introduction to robotics, you study electronics, control engineering, signals and systems, mechanics and industrial robotics, then sensors and actuators, machine learning, computer vision and robot programming, and finally human-robot interaction, collaborative and soft robotics, cybersecurity and ethics. Special laboratories, small-group practicals, robotics projects and optional internships form the practical side, with electives such as deep learning and biomedical robotics, and a bachelor thesis. Graduates work in industrial automation, robot manufacturing, aerospace, hospitals and research institutes, and engineering consultancies.

name: Administración y Dirección de Empresas (ADE) (en inglés)
overview: The business administration core is combined with a choice of specialisation in accounting, business management, finance or marketing, which appears on the final degree, and a range of optional courses including an external internship. First-year students receive mentoring, an internship office supports placements, and a four-year dual degree with a university in Berlin is available. Typical first-year courses include accounting, economics, mathematics and statistics, with business law, finance, marketing and strategy later on. Graduates usually take positions of responsibility in private companies and public organisations in Spain and abroad.

name: Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering
overview: The first year covers calculus, linear algebra, applied physics, mechanics, materials chemistry, construction law and urbanism, then vector calculus, numerical methods, strength of materials, hydraulics and geomatics, and later reinforced concrete, steel structures, soil mechanics, hydrology and transport infrastructure. Fourth-year electives, over thirty in number, let you focus on maritime works, geotechnics, sustainability, smart cities, renewable energy, water management or urban logistics, and a bachelor thesis closes the degree. Graduates work as designers, managers, consultants and builders in infrastructure, transport, ports, water and renewable energy.

name: Bachelor's degree in Bioinformatics (interuniversity UPC-UB-UAB-UPF degree)
overview: The first years cover algebra, calculus, programming, cell biology, biochemistry, molecular biology and computer architecture, then databases, biostatistics, genetics and discrete mathematics, and finally machine learning, computational genomics, structural bioinformatics, phylogenomics and high-performance computing. Electives such as cancer genetics, pharmacology and cloud computing broaden the picture. Courses combine theory with lab work and data analysis projects, and a bachelor's thesis closes the degree. Four Catalan universities run it together, coordinated from the Barcelona School of Informatics. Graduates work in biomedicine, research, pharmacology, R&D, data analysis, AI and quality control, or in academia.

name: Bachelor's degree in Industrial Technologies and Economic Analysis (interuniversity UPC-UPF degree)
overview: Industrial engineering and economics are studied together, beginning with mathematics, physics, chemistry, programming, introductory economics and game theory, then mechanics, materials science, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, microeconomics, macroeconomics and econometrics. Electives range from applied machine learning and optimisation to computational marketing and experimental economics. Taught in English, it includes innovation projects in placements at companies and a bachelor's thesis, and continues into a master's in industrial engineering. Graduates supervise projects, plants and technology centres in energy, chemicals, automotive and robotics, or work in strategic planning and quality management.

name: Bachelor's degree in Video Game Design and Development (taught in English)
overview: The first year mixes programming, mathematics, physics, 3D modelling, design basics and the games industry; later years add game development, game design, 2D animation, concept art, business fundamentals, game engines, artificial intelligence, level design, digital audio and marketing. Teaching is project-based throughout, with multidisciplinary game projects done alone and in groups, optional industrial training and a bachelor's thesis. Electives include virtual and augmented reality, serious games and entrepreneurship, all taught in English. Graduates work as game programmers, designers, producers, 3D artists, animators and gamification consultants.

name: Bachelor's degree in International Business Economics
overview: The first year gives a base in mathematics, company law and financial accounting, and the second goes deeper into microeconomics, macroeconomics, probability, statistics, econometrics and financial analysis, with later work on international trade, marketing and strategy. Teaching is a weekly mix of lectures and seminars, a study period abroad is compulsory, preferably in an English-speaking country, and an optional internship must be abroad or with an international company. Many credits are optional, so there are no fixed tracks, and a final project closes the degree. Graduates work as international market advisers, business consultants, auditors, sales and marketing directors, or in European and international bodies.

name: Bachelor's degree in Global Studies
overview: The degree studies the cultural, economic, legal, environmental, political, social and technological forces of a global society from a transdisciplinary angle, with attention to challenges such as climate change, migration, artificial intelligence, economic crises, war, poverty and pandemics. The first two years are in English, with three compulsory courses in a further language chosen from Chinese, Arabic, Russian, French or Spanish, and later electives can be taken in English, Spanish or Catalan. A stay abroad is compulsory in the third or fourth year, with a double degree option with an Australian university, and optional internships range from government bodies and the European Parliament to think tanks and companies.

name: Bachelor's degree in Industrial Technologies and Economic Analysis
overview: Industrial engineering subjects and the fundamentals of economics are combined, so you learn how technology and processes work and how businesses and markets respond to them. The programme is shared by two Barcelona universities, taught entirely in English across both campuses, and offers optional extracurricular internships on innovation projects at national and international companies. A third language must also be demonstrated. It leads directly into the master's in industrial engineering that qualifies for the regulated profession, or into advanced economics. Graduates manage projects, plants and technology centres in energy, chemicals, robotics, automotive and rail, or work in strategic planning, quality and environmental management.

name: Bachelor's degree in Computer Engineering
overview: A science-based computer engineering curriculum covers the technologies behind everyday applications, including virtual and augmented reality, data science, cybersecurity, machine learning and computational genetics. You can study the whole degree in English, or in a mix of Catalan, Spanish and English, with most third- and fourth-year teaching in English. Optional internships in companies start in the third year, exchanges are open from the third year, a final project closes the degree, and a double degree option is available. Graduates work as cybersecurity experts, web and mobile developers, software and hardware engineers, game developers, tech consultants and IT project managers.

name: Bachelor's Degree in Computational Audiovisual Engineering
overview: The degree trains engineers to design and build audio, video and multimedia systems, weighing cost, quality, security and time in their decisions and keeping the human, legal and ethical sides of the work in view. The first year is largely shared with the other information-technology degrees at the school, and you can take the whole degree in English or in a mix of Catalan, Spanish and English. Optional external internships start in the third year, with companies from broadcasters to technology firms, exchanges are open from the third year, and a final project closes the degree. Graduates work in video and radio production, recording studios, broadcasting, the music, film and video game industries, and computer vision companies.

name: Bachelor's degree in Telecommunications Network Engineering
overview: You learn to conceive, design, manage and operate networks, protocols and multimedia telecommunication services, with the aim of making technical decisions on cost, quality, security and time. Elective tracks in audiovisual systems, software engineering, or business management and innovation let you tailor the later years. You can study entirely in English, optional internships with companies start in the third year, exchanges abroad are open from the third year, and a final project closes the degree. Graduates work in network development, mobile applications, cybersecurity, robotics and drones, research centres, multimedia and internet companies, and network operators.

name: Bachelor's degree in Mathematical Engineering in Data Science
overview: The degree is built on mathematics and computing for making sense of the large volumes of data that social networks, personalised medicine, recommendation systems and smart cities produce. The first year is largely shared with the school's other information-technology degrees, which makes a second degree possible with little extra time. You can take the whole degree in English, optional internships start in the third year, exchanges abroad are open from the third year, and a final project closes the degree. Graduates work as data analysts, machine learning specialists, software developers and AI engineers.

name: Double Bachelor's Degree: Bachelor of Laws (KCL) + Bachelor Degree in Law (UPF)
overview: Two legal traditions are studied in one degree: English common law in the first two years in London, then Spanish law in the last two in Barcelona, with two transition modules in Spanish private and criminal law before the main courses. You learn to analyse conflicts, argue and negotiate, interpret sources of law in both systems, and compare how the two work, using legal language in English and in Spanish or Catalan. External internships can be arranged in the third and fourth years in Barcelona. Graduates can follow careers such as lawyer, solicitor, judge, notary, diplomat, international civil servant, legal consultant or NGO adviser, though many of these need further training and national exams.
